label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: Draw the day as states and it is very simple.
findings.why: Lines 17 to 19 run short declaratives together ('That is the whole design of the brake. One transition anyone can take...'), where one longer sentence could carry the thought.

findings.quote: That is real defence. It had plans amended. It found slips.
findings.why: Three short sentences in a row, and for a reader who wants the record behind every line, 'found slips' gives no count or pointer.

findings.quote: These agents had an insider's reach.
findings.why: Line 5 already asked 'These agents had an insider's reach. What contained them?'; the same sentence is told again as if new.

findings.quote: That line is the whole chapter in one sentence.
findings.why: Chapter 6 (line 156) says 'this whole chapter turns on it' about the same slide quote, so the line is introduced and praised twice across the book.

findings.quote: who may lift it when I am away is written down before it is needed. Until it is, nobody does.
findings.why: I cannot tell whether such a name is written down in this team or not; for a builder deciding who signs, this is the key control and it reads as a conditional.

findings.quote: that session carried it out at my instruction
findings.why: Who held the lift is blurred ('another member's session'); a reader worried about a rubber-stamping editor cannot tell whether the editor himself signed.

findings.quote: six attempts, each refused or failed, one of them only probable, and nothing acted
findings.why: 'Only probable' is unexplained in the text; the count is sourced in the notes but the sentence alone leaves me unsure what a probable attempt is.

findings.quote: Two readers who never compared notes reached the same sequence.
findings.why: The historian line at 28 ('Two readers, no notes shared, the same day to the second') and the figure at 30 say the same finding a third time, and line 106 a fourth.

findings.quote: Both read the hold the same way: part one final, not locked.
findings.why: 'The hold', 'part one final' and 'locked' are used here as settled terms; a newcomer to the book (or this chapter on its own) has not been given them.

findings.quote: the two commits that never reached the team's branch
findings.why: Jargon without a gloss ('commits', 'team's branch') in a paragraph that is a list of things the blind team could not see; I skim it.

findings.quote: That is the point: a team of agents you cannot read is a team you cannot trust.
findings.why: A 'That is the point' opening, and it states a claim that the chapter then shows rather than needs saying.

findings.quote: Every passage marked "shortened from the historian's reconstruction" is the historian's reading of that agent's record
findings.why: This bold paragraph tangles three authors (agent, historian, writer) in one sentence; I stall on whose words the first-person interviews are, which matters to someone exacting about sources.

findings.quote: It does not stop an agent that has been talked into doing something else
findings.why: Chapter 18 (line 34) explains the same scope-versus-steered-agent point in almost the same words, so the explanation is given twice.

findings.quote: The storyteller came late, with a map.
findings.why: The narrator introduces members as a reporter would (lines 109, 118, 127, 136), with no 'I' and no hindsight.

what_holds: 18-how-do-we-contain-this.md: the hold with 'anyone stops, only the editor restarts' answers my question about who signs, and the chapter admits what was thin (the empty security chair, the locks never turned).
06-roles-as-a-cast-you-can-read.md: saying plainly that nobody asked the agents and that the interviews are the historian's reconstruction is the sourcing honesty I look for.
19-a-second-team-reading-cold.md: the one-way valve and the six things the blind team found that this team missed make the checking credible.
notes: Quotes checked against the files before writing. As a newsroom builder I want the signature as control: the editor-only restart is clear, but the stand-in when the editor is away is left open.
